newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oil bill to go to panel vote Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oil bill to go to panel vote Wednesday.

text.p: A Brazilian lower house committee was due to vote Wednesday on a bill regulating the opening up of the petroleum industry, officials said.
The officials said the panel Tuesday discussed the bill prepared by Deputy Eliseu Resende and he had agreed to make changes to the wording of four articles before putting it to a vote Wednesday.
Resende told reporters panel members had proposed 100 amendments to the bill but because many were similar, he expected only 30 changes to be voted on.
Congress approved in 1995 the end of state oil firm Petrobras' monopoly but legislators have yet to pass the regulatory laws to put it into practice.
Resende's bill would allow private firms to compete against or go into partnership with Petrobras.
After the panel vote, due to start at 1000 local time/1300 GMT, the bill is likely to go for a vote on the full floor of the lower house, perhaps next week.

The committee does have the authority to vote in the name of the full Chamber of Deputies and to pass the bill on to the upper house. But opposition parties say they will insist on a vote on the floor before the bill heads to the Senate.
